title: Explicit localized polynomial image in a local algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $B$ a commutative local $k$-algebra, $A_0\subseteq B$ a $k$-subalgebra, and $x\in B$. Define $\theta:A_0[T]\to B$ by inclusion on coefficients and $T\mapsto x$. Put $P=\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$, which is prime. The localized polynomial image is $A=\operatorname{im}(A_0[T]_P\to B)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], where evaluation extends because every polynomial outside $P$ has unit image. This specifies the subalgebra itself, rather than an unspecified witness. It is local, contains $A_0$ and $x$, and is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] whenever $A_0$ is.

source.place: Tag 07FI, transcendental case: localization of the polynomial evaluation map and its image; admissibility from Tag 07FH. Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FI and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH.

proof.text: The complement of P consists precisely of polynomials whose evaluations are units. Extend evaluation by the localization universal property and take its k-algebra range. Constants show A₀ ≤ A and T shows x ∈ A. A is a nontrivial quotient of the local ring A₀[T]_P, so is local.

If A₀ is essentially of finite type over k, compose its structure map with the polynomial extension and localization; both are essentially of finite type. The surjection to the image preserves essential finite type.
